name: zlib-ng via flate2 (libz-ng-sys backend)
baseline: flate2 1.1 with its default miniz_oxide backend, streaming inflate and deflate in 4096-byte chunks
verdict_reason: Compression gains are large (2.1x to 2.7x at level 6), but inflate is only 1.17x faster on Zen 4 and no faster on Apple M4, where it ties miniz_oxide at 416 MB/s. zlib-rs matches or beats it on inflate without a C build.
tier_reason: Public flate2 harness run by developers outside the zlib-ng project, with rustc and LLVM versions and CPUs stated.
claimed_speedup: Level-6 deflate 37.848 vs 13.772 MB/s on Zen 4 (2.75x) and 47.464 vs 22.074 MB/s on Apple M4 (2.15x); inflate 621.911 vs 533.374 MB/s on Zen 4 (1.17x) and 416.191 vs 416.072 MB/s on M4 (1.00x); author's own run: inflate 578.741 vs 487.149 MB/s (1.19x), level-6 deflate 32.303 vs 11.960 MB/s (2.70x) (ratios derived from page data).
workload: silesia-small.tar through flate2's streaming API in 4096-byte chunks: inflate, and deflate at levels 1, 6 and 9; mean wall time per run.
hardware: AMD Zen 4 desktop and Apple M4; unnamed x86_64 Linux machine (second run)
toolchain: rustc 1.97.0-nightly (2026-04-12), LLVM 22.1.2; zlib-ng built from source by libz-ng-sys (run logs list Ubuntu clang 14.0.0 on Zen 4 and Apple clang 21 on M4)
platforms: Targets zlib-ng supports with a C toolchain; needs CMake unless the experimental cc-based build feature is enabled
one_liner: flate2's zlib-ng C backend: level-6 deflate 2.1x to 2.7x faster than miniz_oxide; inflate gains are small to none.
how_it_is_fast: zlib-ng is a modernized zlib fork with SIMD checksums, SIMD string matching and faster deflate strategies per level, selected by runtime CPU detection. flate2 links it natively (not in zlib-compat mode) through libz-ng-sys.
use_it_when: Compression throughput matters and a C toolchain with CMake is already in the build
Other parts of the dependency graph already link zlib-ng
skip_it_when: You mostly decompress: zlib-rs is faster on inflate in the same runs and needs no C build
You cross-compile to targets where building C with CMake is painful (wasm, some Windows setups)
Tests pin exact compressed bytes or sizes
caveats: Nightly rustc in both runs; the C side's compiler differed between machines
On Apple M4 inflate was a tie with miniz_oxide
tradeoffs: C code parsing untrusted input, outside Rust's memory-safety checks
Build needs CMake or an experimental cc-based feature
Different compression ratios from miniz_oxide at some levels (1.846 vs 1.991 at level 1 in these runs)
